last.minutes: The broader altcoin market remains defensive while Bitcoin consolidates above key levels, supporting our disciplined spot posture. We maintain our core spot holdings in BTC, AAVE, and SOL, trimming AAVE slightly to 28% to strictly enforce our 30% single-asset concentration rule without generating excessive churn. In the futures book, we hold the winning short QNT position at 2x leverage, supported by weakening technical momentum and validated quant performance.

futures.why: QNT exhibits sharp downside momentum and strong quant validation, making the profitable short worth holding.

spot.why: AAVE displays strong technical buying interest but is trimmed slightly to adhere to the 30% concentration cap.
Bitcoin maintains relative strength and macro tailwinds amidst softer U.S. yields.
Holding SOL within disciplined risk limits avoids premature tax friction and transaction costs.

lessons.text: Trimming positions only when necessary for risk compliance, such as enforcing the 30% single-coin limit, prevents regulatory breaches while protecting the portfolio from excessive transaction fees and tax drag.
Strictly adhering to portfolio concentration limits while cutting underperforming leveraged positions protects capital from unnecessary drawdown and tax drag.
Minimizing unnecessary adjustments to our spot holdings avoids triggering the 31.2% tax and high transaction fees, while selective shorting in futures can exploit clear relative weakness.
Strict adherence to portfolio concentration limits and disciplined risk management protects capital from fee drag and excess volatility in a risk-off market.

Prioritizing regulatory compliance through minor rebalancing while resisting the urge to churn underperforming but within-limit positions helps preserve capital against high Indian tax and transaction costs.
Proactively trimming winning spot assets to respect the 30% single-asset limit ensures compliance while avoiding the heavy fee and tax drag of wholesale portfolio turnover.
